NEW DELHI: In a major setback to the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in Punjab, three of its MLAs, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday, ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.The three leaders reached the BJP headquarters in Delhi for the formal induction. A video shared by news agency ANI showed Pathanmajra and Jouramajra raising slogans of 'BJP zindabad' at the party office.The induction comes after Pathanmajra and Jouramajra resigned from the AAP's primary membership on Sunday, while Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, a suspended AAP MLA and former IPS officer, resigned from the Punjab assembly on Monday before joining the BJP.The three leaders are Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, who represents Amritsar North, Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour in Punjab's Patiala district.The development comes at a crucial time for the AAP, which is preparing for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. The party announced its first list of 40 candidates on Saturday, naming Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann from Dhuri, Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan from Kotkapura and jailed minister Sanjeev Arora from Ludhiana West.Neither Samana nor Sanour figured in the list.Pathanmajra and Jouramajra had accused the Bhagwant Mann-led government of failing to address several issues, including the drug menace, rising state debt and governance-related concerns.Jouramajra, a former Punjab minister, had criticised the government's handling of the drug problem and raised the cases of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was killed in Mansa, and Dalit man Gulzar Singh, who died by suicide in Sangrur.He also questioned the government's failure to fulfil its promise of providing minimum support price for crops and alleged a shortage of teachers in government schools.Pathanmajra, meanwhile, accused AAP leaders from Delhi of controlling the Punjab government, claiming that state ministers did not have the authority to approve even a single file independently.Following their resignations, the AAP said it would approach the Punjab Assembly Speaker seeking cancellation of their legislative membership, alleging that both leaders had engaged in anti-party activities. The party had suspended the two MLAs before they quit.Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, a former IPS officer and MLA from Amritsar North, resigned from the Punjab Assembly on Monday before joining the BJP.He submitted his resignation to Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and announced the decision in a Facebook post."I have resigned from the membership of Punjab Vidhan Sabha," Singh posted.In his resignation letter to the Speaker, he wrote, "I hereby tender my resignation of my seat in the House with effect from 1.11.2026."Singh was suspended from the AAP for five years in June 2025 over alleged anti-party activities. His suspension followed his criticism of the Punjab Vigilance Bureau's action against Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia, who was arrested in a disproportionate assets case.A former member of the Punjab Police special investigation team (SIT) that probed the 2015 Kotkapura and Behbal Kalan police-firing incidents, Singh had repeatedly questioned the Mann government's handling of the sacrilege cases.The BJP's induction of the three leaders has drawn criticism from the AAP leadership. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora accused the BJP of attempting to induct leaders who had left or been expelled from other parties.AAP chief spokesperson Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal had also described the BJP as a 'kabaad di dukaan' (scrap shop), accusing it of collecting rejected political faces.Before resigning, Pathanmajra had said that he would join a party that worked in the interest of Punjab.Jouramajra served in the Bhagwant Mann cabinet from January 2023 to September 2024 before being dropped during a cabinet reshuffle.
Article Summary: Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh join BJP. The three leaders reached the BJP headquarters in Delhi for the formal induction. The AAP said it would approach the Punjab Assembly Speaker seeking cancellation of their legislative membership.

Article Title: 6 Indian trekkers 'ignore weather warnings', get stranded in Nepal
Article Text:
Six Indian trekkers remain stranded in Nepal's snowbound Upper Dolpa region after continuing their trek despite weather warnings, with a helicopter technical fault delaying rescue efforts

Six Indian trekkers, including four men and two women, remained stranded in Nepal's snowbound Upper Dolpa region Sunday after allegedly ignoring weather warnings and leaving their guide behind to continue towards Shey-Phoksundo Lake. A technical fault in a Nepal Army helicopter delayed rescue efforts, while heavy snowfall linked to Cyclone Arnab made mountain trails inaccessible.The six - Moumita Halder, Piyali Koley, Jajla Trivedi Kumar, Aditya Singha, Diplina Biswas and Rajesh De - got stranded on Saturday afternoon in Danigad, roughly 300km northwest of Kathmandu. Their destination, Shey-Phoksundo Lake, lies at an altitude of about 3,600 metres and is considered Nepal's deepest lake, with an estimated depth of 145 metres.Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology had warned of rain, heavy snow and avalanche risks between Oct 29 and 31, prompting restrictions on high-altitude travel. Dolpa chief district officer Junu Hamal Dhakal said, "The group continued towards the lake despite warnings from security personnel and their Nepalese guide about worsening weather. They left the guide behind and pressed ahead as snowfall intensified, disregarding restrictions the district administration had imposed on travel towards Upper Dolpa.Locals also warned them that heavy snow could make the mountain passes impassable."The guide alerted authorities on Saturday evening after losing contact with the trekkers. By Sunday morning, the administration had mobilised security personnel and sought helicopter assistance. "We have located the area where they are stranded, and an Army helicopter is arriving to rescue them. We hope to rescue them soon," Dhakal said.However, the helicopter stationed at Surkhet air base could not take off because of a technical fault, forcing authorities to arrange another aircraft. "Rescue initiatives are continuing with the use of a Nepal Army helicopter. However, telephone contact is not viable with the tourists as there is no mobile network in the area where they are stranded," Dhakal said.
Article Summary: Six Indian trekkers, including four men and two women, remain stranded in Nepal's snowbound Upper Dolpa region. They allegedly ignored weather warnings and left their guide behind to continue towards Shey-Phoksundo Lake. A technical fault in a Nepal Army helicopter delayed rescue efforts, while heavy snowfall linked to Cyclone Arnab made mountain trails inaccessible.

Article Title: 'No military solutions': EAM Jaishankar reveals PM Modi-Putin talks on Ukraine conflict in Delhi, Bishkek
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi with Russian President Vladimir Putin

India focuses on civilian shipping, grain exports and energy security

Jaishankar calls for diplomatic solutions to global conflicts

Jaishankar meets Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has said Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed the Ukraine conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin in New Delhi and earlier in Bishkek, as India continues diplomatic engagement with Moscow, Kyiv and Washington on measures to protect civilian shipping, restore grain exports and safeguard energy infrastructure.Speaking exclusively to news agency ANI on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta on Saturday, Jaishankar said India had held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on three key aspects of the conflict."Prime Minister himself had a discussion with President Putin in Delhi and before that in Bishkek," he said, referring to India's diplomatic engagement.Jaishankar said he had also discussed the conflict with Russian and Ukrainian officials, including during visits to Moscow and Kyiv, and in talks with Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov."We have also been coordinating this with the Americans because they have their own peace mediation initiative. So Secretary Rubio knows properly what is going on here," he said.Explaining the three areas under discussion, Jaishankar said India was first seeking to ensure that civilian vessels and seafarers were not targeted in the conflict.The second priority was to restore grain exports from Russia and Ukraine, both major suppliers to international markets.He said shipments through the Black Sea had fallen sharply because of the conflict."One not to attack civilian shipping and seafarers. The second is to find a way by which the grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine. Then these are two major exporters of grains for the global markets. Find a way of restoring that flow because that flow has cut down very sharply in the Black Sea," he said.The third area concerned energy infrastructure and shipments. Jaishankar said this was the most complicated issue because the concerns differed among the parties involved."Non-attack on energy is probably the most complicated piece because it means different things to the different players," he said, referring to refineries, electricity grids and ships carrying fuel.He added that India was trying to bring the parties together to address these concerns but could not publicly disclose the current status of the discussions.At the G20 meeting, the external affairs minister reiterated India's position that major international conflicts required diplomatic engagement rather than military escalation."Look, there are big conflicts today, two major conflicts which are having global ramifications," he said, adding that "there are no military solutions; we have to find a diplomatic pathway."Jaishankar also flagged the impact of disruptions in energy markets and fuel distribution on developing economies."This distortion of the energy markets, the politicisation of energy flows, this is something which is very harmful," he said, adding that the Global South was bearing the brunt of energy shortages.He also raised concerns over disruptions to grain shipments through the Black Sea and fertiliser shortages linked to tensions along the Persian Gulf and Red Sea corridors.On supply chain resilience, which was the focus of the G20 meeting's concluding plenary session, Jaishankar called for greater diversification of global production and manufacturing networks."Today we need more diversified supply chains," he said, advocating "more globalised, you know, more diversified production, more diversified manufacturing."In a post on X after the session, he said securing resilient supply chains was central to the well-being of the global economy. He also called for promoting the "right to industrialise", resisting "predatory practices" and pursuing the "de-politicisation of markets".On the sidelines of the G20 meeting, Jaishankar held separate discussions with his Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts on the Ukraine conflict, West Asia, bilateral ties and multilateral issues.After meeting Lavrov, Jaishankar said the two sides had discussed the Ukraine conflict, the Gulf situation and multilateral issues.He also met Polish Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, with discussions focusing on the Ukraine conflict, India-European Union ties and the G20."My meeting with DPM & FM Radosław Sikorski @sikorskiradek of Poland focused on the Ukraine conflict, India-EU ties and the G20," Jaishankar said.Poland is participating in this year's G20 meetings as a full participant following an invitation from the United States. It has also expressed interest in securing permanent membership of the grouping.Jaishankar separately met South Korean foreign minister Cho Hyun to review bilateral cooperation and discuss G20-related and other multilateral issues."Appreciated the stocktaking with @FMChoHyun of the Republic of Korea of our bilateral cooperation, as also the discussion on G20 and multilateral issues," he said.Earlier on Saturday, Jaishankar also participated in the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta with US secretary of state Marco Rubio, Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian foreign minister Penny Wong.The US is holding the G20 presidency this year. After two days of discussions, Jaishankar and other foreign ministers attended a college football game between the Florida Gators and the Georgia Bulldogs at the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.
Article Summary: India continues diplomatic engagement with Moscow, Kyiv and Washington on measures to protect civilian shipping, restore grain exports and safeguard energy infrastructure. External affairs minister reiterated India's position that major international conflicts required diplomatic engagement rather than military escalation. Jaishankar held separate discussions with his Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts on the Ukraine conflict.

Article Title: 'Remarkable valour': PM Modi pays tribute to Haryana's heritage on foundation day
Article Text:
Celebrating its 60th Foundation Day on November 1, Haryana showcased its rich heritage and remarkable achievements. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Amit Shah, Rahul Gandhi extend greetings

Haryana marks six decades of statehood

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday extended greetings to the people of Haryana as the state marked 60 years since its formation, praising its rich cultural heritage, sporting achievements and contributions to the country's growth.In a message posted on X, PM Modi highlighted Haryana's glorious history, courage and vibrant rural traditions, noting that its folk culture has played an important role in enriching India's cultural identity."Heartiest congratulations and best wishes to all my family members of the state on Haryana Day! Our state, adorned with a glorious history, remarkable valor, and a rich culture, is the pride of the nation. The folk traditions and vibrant rural culture here have always enriched the nation's cultural heritage," the Prime Minister wrote.PM Modi also acknowledged the contributions of Haryana's athletes and farmers, saying they have brought recognition to the country on international platforms and strengthened its food security."The people of Haryana have proven their talent and determination from agriculture, sports, and defence services to industry, education, and startups through their hard work and dedication.The athletes here are enhancing the honour of the tricolour, while the food providers are strengthening the country's food security. I wish that this special occasion brings prosperity into the lives of all the people here," he added.Union home minister Amit Shah also conveyed his wishes to Haryana's residents, describing the state as a land of courage, hard work and prosperity. In his message on X, he highlighted its contributions to national security, sports, agriculture and animal husbandry."Heartfelt greetings to all the residents of the state on the Foundation Day of Haryana, the land of valor, labour, and prosperity. Be it defending the nation on the borders, enhancing the honour of the tricolour on the sports fields, or setting new benchmarks in agriculture and animal husbandry, Haryana's contribution in every field is unparalleled," Amit Shah wrote.He further praised the state's soldiers, sportspersons and farmers for their role in strengthening India's reputation and economic progress, expressing hope that Haryana would continue to advance.Leader of the opposition in the lok sabha Rahul Gandhi also extended greetings to people across several states and union territories celebrating their foundation days on November 1.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi highlighted the country's diverse cultural traditions, languages and regional identities, saying they have shaped India's national character. He wished the regions continued prosperity and progress while contributing to a united nation.The Congress party also issued greetings to residents of Haryana and other states and Union territories marking their formation anniversaries. It called for continued progress, unity and commitment to constitutional values.At the state level, chief minister Nayab Singh Saini attended the foundation day celebrations in Chandigarh, marking six decades since Haryana became a separate state on November 1, 1966.Recalling the state's journey, Saini acknowledged the contributions of those who had campaigned for its formation and worked towards its development."We express our gratitude to all the great personalities who struggled for the formation of Haryana and worked hard for the construction of modern Haryana. On this day in 1966, when it became a separate state, it was very backward. Our farmer benefactors, hardworking labourers, diligent industrialists and traders, and valiant sportspersons all made a significant contribution in transforming that backward region into a modern, developed Haryana," the chief minister said.Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Punjab and Tamil Nadu observe their state formation day on November 1. Several union territories, including Chandigarh, Delhi, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lakshadweep, also mark their foundation day on the occasion.
Article Summary: Haryana marks six decades of statehood on November 1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to the people of Haryana. He praised its rich cultural heritage, sporting achievements and contributions to the country's growth. Union home minister Amit Shah also conveyed his wishes to the state's residents.

Article Title: US midterm elections 2026: What they are, why they matter and when results will be out
Article Text:
US midterms voting to be conducted on November 3

What are the US midterm elections?

What is at stake in the 2026 midterms?

Why do the midterms matter for Trump?

What issues are shaping the vote?

When will voting take place and when will results come?

Where can you check the results?

US Election Assistance Commission (EAC): A federal agency that provides election information and links to official state election offices.

USA.gov: The US government's official portal, which directs users to state websites for election results and voting information.

Federal Election Commission (FEC): The federal agency responsible for campaign finance oversight. It provides information on federal elections but does not publish live results or certify current election outcomes.

What happens if an election result is contested?

The US midterm elections are nationwide elections held every two years, halfway through a president's four-year term. This year's elections will take place on November 3 with voters choosing members of Congress as well as several state and local officials.Unlike presidential elections, midterms do not decide who occupies the White House. Instead, they determine which party controls Congress for the next two years, making them a crucial test of President Donald Trump's political standing and his ability to push through his agenda.The US Congress has two chambers, the House of Representatives and the Senate, and midterm elections determine the composition of both. All 435 seats in the House are contested every two years, as members serve two-year terms.In the Senate, where members serve six-year terms, roughly one-third of the 100 seats come up for election every two years. This time, 35 Senate seats, including two special-election contests, are at stake. Alongside congressional races, voters in several states will also elect governors and other state and local officials.Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers of Congress.The 435-member House has 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one independent who caucuses with Republicans and two vacant seats. A party needs 218 seats for a majority.Meanwhile, the Senate has 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats and allied independents, with 51 seats required for a majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in each chamber to take control of both.The outcome could therefore hinge on a small number of closely contested races.The party controlling Congress has considerable influence over the president's ability to govern.Congress passes legislation, approves government spending and oversees the executive branch. The Senate also confirms presidential nominees to key government positions, including federal judges and senior administration officials.If Democrats take control of either chamber, they could make it harder for Trump to pass legislation, influence budget negotiations and intensify congressional scrutiny of his administration through hearings and investigations.A Democratic majority in the House could also revive discussions of impeachment, although impeachment by itself would not remove the president from office. Removal requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate.Trump would remain president regardless of the election outcome. He would retain his executive powers and the ability to veto legislation, but a divided Congress could significantly constrain his domestic agenda.The cost of living, inflation, immigration and the economy are among the major concerns for voters. Foreign policy, including the war involving Iran, is also part of the political debate.Trump's approval ratings and public perceptions of his administration's performance are likely to influence the results. Midterm elections are often viewed as a referendum on the sitting president, with the party in the White House frequently losing congressional seats.Disputes over voting rules, election administration and the drawing of congressional district boundaries have also become contentious issues.Voting will take place on Tuesday, November 3, across the United States. Polling hours vary by state, and there is no single nationwide closing time.The first polling stations in parts of Indiana and Kentucky are scheduled to close at 6 pm Eastern Time, which is around 4.30 am on November 4 as per Indian Standard Time.Results are expected to emerge through the night, but close contests may take longer to resolve. Election officials must count outstanding ballots, verify results and, where necessary, conduct recounts or deal with legal challenges.News organisations may project winners before every ballot has been counted. Such projections are not official results. State election authorities certify the final results, a process that can take days or weeks.State election offices remain the primary source for official results, including vote counts, recounts and final certification.A close result can lead to recounts, court challenges and disputes over ballot validity. State officials handle the initial counting and certification process, but the US Constitution gives the House and Senate the power to judge the elections, returns and qualifications of their own members.A candidate or sitting member can challenge a congressional election result. In the House, such disputes are referred to the House Administration Committee, while Senate challenges go to the Senate Rules Committee. The respective chamber ultimately decides whether a member should be seated.This power could become significant if a handful of unresolved races determine which party controls Congress. Any House contests still unresolved when the new Congress convenes in January would be considered by the incoming House.The process can become politically contentious, particularly when party control is at stake. A disputed result may also leave a seat vacant while legal or congressional proceedings continue.
Article Summary: Voting will take place on Tuesday, November 3, across the United States. Polling hours vary by state, and there is no single nationwide closing time. Results are expected to emerge through the night, but close contests may take longer to resolve.

Article Title: Philadelphia professor arrested for blocking delivery robots, says she would do it again because she believes she has more rights than a robot
Article Text:
Retired professor has been arrested for blocking a delivery robot in Philadelphia.

Why delivery robots have legal protection

A 78-year-old retired professor in Philadelphia has vowed to continue protesting delivery robots after she was arrested for repeatedly standing in their way, arguing that her actions were an exercise of free speech and a protest against technology taking over public spaces.Carolyn Marvin, a retired communications professor at the University of Pennsylvania, said blocking autonomous delivery robots had become a habit since the small, wheeled machines began operating on Philadelphia’s streets and sidewalks.October 14 was not the first time Marvin had placed herself in front of one of the robots. She would stop them for a few minutes as they travelled along the sidewalk carrying food orders.“I was under the impression that I had more rights than the robot did,” Marvin said to CNN in an inerview.The October 14 incident ended with her arrest. Marvin said she had been returning home after getting a flu shot when she encountered a delivery robot. She had a jar of enchilada sauce in one hand and chicken biryani takeout in the other when she stood in front of the machine, as she had done on previous occasions.The incident took place in a busy part of the city, and a larger-than-usual crowd gathered.Some people supported her, while others criticized her. Marvin suspects someone in the crowd eventually called the police.Officers handcuffed her, put her in a police vehicle and issued her a citation for disorderly conduct.Philadelphia police said they had responded to a report of “criminal mischief involving a delivery robot”. When officers arrived, they found a woman “who was refusing to allow a delivery robot to pass”, according to an email from the police department. Officers issued multiple commands asking her to move, but she refused to comply.Marvin said she never expected to be arrested because she believed she was not obstructing another person.“I wasn’t impeding any persons. I was impeding a machine,” she said.She described her actions as a symbolic protest against the problems associated with delivery robots, including the displacement of low-income delivery workers, the physical risks the machines could pose to people using sidewalks and privacy concerns arising from their built-in cameras.“I also think that I have a First Amendment right to protest the abuses of corporations in public space, in the same public space that the robots are occupying,” she said.Marvin said she had previously taken part in protests supporting civil rights and abortion rights, supporting Black Lives Matter and opposing the Gulf and Vietnam wars. She sees her campaign against delivery robots as an extension of the same impulse to make the government hear public concerns.She said blocking the machines had also led to conversations with passersby who wanted to know what she was doing. Most were supportive or curious.Marvin said her protest had a limited impact on customers, with an office worker’s lunch potentially delayed by around 15 minutes at most. She added that she did not have unlimited time to spend blocking robots and would do so for 10 or 15 minutes when it was “convenient and possible”.A friend summed up her arrest by telling her: “Well, you got a disorderly conduct charge for impeding capitalism.”Following her arrest, Marvin learnt more about the legal framework governing autonomous delivery devices in Pennsylvania.In 2020, the state legislature passed a law classifying autonomous delivery robots, described in the legislation as “personal delivery devices”, as pedestrians rather than vehicles.The legislation was largely opposed by Democrats, labour unions and accessibility advocates, who argued that allowing delivery robots could threaten jobs and put children and pedestrians at risk. Republicans supported the measure, describing it as an exciting technological development.The law requires vehicles to yield to delivery robots at crosswalks, just as they would to pedestrians, John Mattiacci, a Philadelphia personal injury attorney told CNN.However, the machines are also required to give way to people and cyclists in pedestrian areas.“Personal delivery devices must yield to other pedestrians and pedalcyclists in a pedestrian area,” Mattiacci said.Uber Eats introduced robot deliveries in Philadelphia in March, making it the fourth city where the company offered the service. However, not everyone has welcomed the robots. Videos recorded in Philadelphia and other cities have shown people sitting on the machines, kicking them and causing damage.Marvin sees the growing presence of delivery robots as part of a wider trend in which technology and machines are increasingly occupying everyday spaces.“There’s a way in which we’ve surrendered the streets to cars long ago, and I don’t think we should surrender the sidewalks to machines,” she said.“Machines in general encroach on our lives,” she added. “Public space is the most visible place where they’re encroaching on our lives, but they’re going right up the ladder, and lots of people are interested in making that happen.”She said robots were a visible symbol of the wider spread of technology, including artificial intelligence and social media algorithms that influence the images and narratives people consume.Her protest, she said, helps make the issue visible and presents it in a way that might otherwise go unnoticed.Asked whether she planned to resume blocking delivery robots after her arrest, Marvin had a brief answer: “Oh yeah.”This time, however, she said she would keep an eye out for the police.
Article Summary: Carolyn Marvin, 78, was arrested for blocking a delivery robot in Philadelphia. She said her actions were an exercise of free speech and a protest against technology taking over public spaces. Marvin said she never expected to be arrested because she believed she was not obstructing another person.

Article Title: A Delaware couple cared for a backyard triangle for over 20 years before neighbours demanded $30,000 to let them keep the fenced land; an October 30 court ruling has now awarded the entire disputed st
Article Text:
Decades of maintenance establishing continuous control

Failed negotiations and monetary demands

Division of the disputed triangular parcel

A long-running property dispute between neighbours in Newark, Delaware, has ended with a court ruling that gives homeowners legal ownership of a piece of land they had looked after for more than 20 years. According to legal documents published by Justia Law, the Delaware Court of Chancery issued a decision in an adverse possession case involving Plaintiffs Joseph W.C. Murray, Jr. and Danielle F. Murray and Defendants Nikola Preradovic, Rade Preradovic, and Zeljka Preradovic. The dispute involved a triangular piece of land along the boundary between two neighbouring homes in New Castle County. The Murrays showed that they had openly, continuously, and exclusively used the enclosed rear part of the disputed land for more than the 20 years required under Delaware law. As a result, the court awarded them full legal ownership of that section.Court records show that the Murrays had looked after the fenced section of land for around 25 years. The family put up fences, maintained the garden, and regularly treated the rear area behind their home as part of their own yard. Over the years, the Murrays placed several personal items inside the fenced area. These included a stone retaining wall, garden features, a beehive, and a decorative statue.Photographs and witness statements presented in court showed that these items had remained there over time. This helped confirm that the family had continued to control and use the rear yard without interruption. Under Delaware property laws, anyone claiming land through adverse possession must prove that their use of the property was open, visible, continuous, exclusive, and against the interests of the legal owner for at least 20 years. The court explained that continuous use does not mean someone must be physically present every minute. Instead, they must act like an owner in a way that suits the type of land involved.The legal dispute began after the Preradovic family bought the neighbouring property at 234 South Dilwyn in December 2022. Soon after buying the property, the new owners noticed differences in the boundary lines after land surveys. They asked the Murrays to move or remove the existing fence. During the first discussions, both sides considered officially changing the property boundaries through New Castle County authorities. However, the talks broke down because they could not agree on the financial terms. Court documents show that the new property owners asked the Murrays to pay $30,000 in exchange for signing a deed transfer that would allow them to keep the fenced land. The Murrays refused to pay and claimed they already had rights to the land because they had used it for many years. The disagreement then led to a formal case in the Court of Chancery. At first, the Murrays asked the court to enforce what they said was an agreement to transfer the land. In an earlier decision, Magistrate in Chancery Loren Mitchell found that the claimed sale agreement could not be legally enforced. This was because both sides had not clearly agreed on the exact legal description of the property. The case then moved forward to a full review of the main adverse possession claim.When reviewing the land and its layout, the Court of Chancery divided the disputed triangular area into three separate sections. These were the enclosed rear yard behind the fence, a stone planter area, and an unfenced grass lawn stretching towards the street. The court decided that the Murrays had met all the legal requirements for adverse possession of the rear section enclosed by the fence and retaining wall. The ruling explained that the fence clearly showed that the family was treating the land as their own. This would have been obvious to anyone who owned or lived on the neighbouring property. However, the court rejected the Murrays' claim to the front sections of the triangular plot. These included the planter area and the front grass strip beside the road. The court found that the family had not maintained these areas regularly. There were periods when the grass became overgrown, and other people also had access to the space. The judge ruled that regularly cutting grass along an unfenced front boundary was not enough to prove exclusive control against the legal owner. Such activity did not meet the legal standard needed to take ownership away from someone who already held the deed. As a result, the court officially awarded the Murrays ownership of the enclosed rear yard. However, the Preradovic family kept legal ownership of the outer front lawn.
Article Summary: The dispute involved a triangular piece of land along the boundary between two neighbouring homes in New Castle County, Delaware. The Murrays showed that they had openly, continuously, and exclusively used the enclosed rear part of the disputed land for more than the 20 years required under Delaware law. As a result, the court awarded them full legal ownership of that section.

Article Title: Princess Catherine’s sister Pippa Middleton and husband James Matthews ordered to demolish unauthorised car park at £15.5 million estate; neighbours raise concerns over construction without consultati
Article Text:
Pippa Middleton and James Matthews have faced criticism from locals over construction and public access to their estate. (Photo: Instagram/Google Maps)

Council rules car park development was visually intrusive

Neighbours objected to construction without consultation

Pippa Middleton and husband James Matthews have been ordered to demolish an unauthorised car park at their £15.5 million estate. (Photo: Instagram)

Pippa Middleton and James Matthews' previous dispute with locals

Pippa Middleton and her hedge fund manager husband, James Matthews, have been ordered to remove a car park they built on their sprawling country estate without obtaining prior planning permission. The decision comes after a group of residents in the picturesque village of Kintbury raised objections with West Berkshire Council, claiming they had not been consulted before construction began last year.Pippa, the younger sister of Princess Catherine, and James own the land, which forms part of their £15.5 million, 145-acre Barton Court estate. The couple moved into the property in 2022 and have since been involved in several disagreements with locals over developments and access to the estate.According to a report by The Times, the couple subsequently applied for retrospective planning permission for the anglers' car park, arguing that the sale of fishing rights along the River Kennet was a significant source of income that helped support the upkeep of the estate.However, West Berkshire Council rejected the proposal, concluding that the development was 'visually intrusive and urbanised' and had 'eroded a measure of the open and undeveloped rural character' of the North Wessex Downs.The couple have now been directed to remove the car park.The development reportedly involved laying approximately 400 square metres of agricultural hard standing across a meadow. The land was previously known among residents as the grazing ground of two heavy horses, Monty and Drummer, who lived there before the estate changed hands.The car park drew considerable criticism from residents, who approached the council after noticing the construction. In objections submitted to the authorities, locals said they were 'shocked' by the development and questioned why the community had not been consulted before work began.Some residents also alleged that the car park had been created to move vehicles away from areas closer to the couple's home, thereby preserving the views around their property.One objector reportedly wrote: 'This application is to move unsightly parking out of sight of the applicants on entry to the Barton Court estate to the detriment of the residents and the heritage of Kintbury.'Another resident highlighted concerns about the location, traffic congestion and the potential impact on the area's heritage, requesting that the planning committee conduct a site inspection before reaching a decision.Planners also raised concerns about the absence of mitigation measures to protect the River Kennet from potential adverse environmental impacts.This is not the first time Pippa and James have found themselves at odds with residents since moving to Barton Court. The couple previously faced opposition after restricting public access to Mill Lane, a route that runs through their estate and had reportedly been used by local dog walkers and ramblers for years.The Grade I-listed Barton Court, situated along the River Kennet near Kintbury, was previously owned by late retail tycoon Sir Terence Conran, who had allowed members of the public to use the lane.However, after Pippa and James moved into the property with their three children, Arthur, Grace and Rose, in 2022, they installed an electric gate to restrict access. Signs reading 'Private: No Public Access' and 'No Trespassing' also appeared around the estate.The move prompted 35 residents, supported by the Ramblers Association, to approach West Berkshire Council, seeking to have Mill Lane officially recognised as a public right of way.A Planning Inspectorate inquiry into the dispute began at the village hall in May. James Matthews also attended the proceedings, where he reportedly argued that the family's security and privacy concerns should be taken into consideration.
Article Summary: Council rules car park development was visually intrusive and urbanised. Neighbours objected to construction without consultation by West Berkshire Council. Couple moved into the property in 2022 and have since been involved in several disagreements with locals over developments and access to the estate.

Article Title: 9 dead as Florida jet crashes near busy roadway
Article Text:
Emergency crews respond after a Learjet 60 crashed into a South Florida neighbourhood, killing all nine people on board

All nine people aboard a business jet were killed after it crashed into a South Florida neighbourhood on Sunday, US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said.The Learjet 60, which departed from Austin, Texas, was headed to the Bahamas when it nose-dived into the neighbourhood and burst into flames. The crash created a large fiery crater in the pavement near a busy roadway, news agency AP reported.The aircraft appeared to narrowly miss nearby homes before crashing, according to initial reports.Duffy said the Federal Aviation Administration was sending a team to assist the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) in investigating the cause of the crash.The circumstances leading to the crash and the identities of those killed were not immediately clear.
Article Summary: The Learjet 60, which departed from Austin, Texas, was headed to the Bahamas when it nose-dived into the neighbourhood and burst into flames. The crash created a large fiery crater in the pavement near a busy roadway. The circumstances leading to the crash and the identities of those killed were not immediately clear.

Article Title: Shutdown in 3 Arunachal Pradesh districts today to oppose Siang mega dam
Article Text:
(Photo credit: PTI) Protest in support of Arunachal anti-dam movement





GUWAHATI: The confrontation over the proposed 11,200MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal escalated Sunday, with a youth organisation calling a shutdown across three districts along the Siang river Monday, demanding the release of those arrested over anti-dam violence and opposing the deployment of 30 CAPF companies in the region.SUMP Affected Area Youth Association (SAAYA) called the bandh after state govt missed a deadline to release more than 40 protesters arrested over the Oct 23 violence in Pasighat and subsequent attacks on security personnel in Siang and Upper Siang."Govt will decide on release of the arrested, but as of Sunday there is no such decision," a police source said.SAAYA had issued the ultimatum at an emergency meeting of affected villages on Oct 29, threatening a shutdown from Nov 2 if the arrested were not released by Nov 1. GURGAON: A journey of a few kilometres towards Delhi turned into an hours long ordeal at Sirhaul border on Sunday as police checks for vehicles barred under the capital’s new pollution curbs brought the Delhi-bound carriageway of the expressway to a near standstill.Cars, buses and two-wheelers were packed into long queues stretching from IFFCO Chowk, with commuters saying they remained stuck at the same spot for 40 minutes to over two hours, barely moving a few hundred metres.The jam was most severe on the carriageway leading to the capital, while traffic in the opposite direction flowed relatively smoothly. Buses packed with passengers were caught in the gridlock. Two-wheeler riders, usually able to weave through slow-moving traffic, found little room to manoeuvre. Some commuters eventually abandoned their cabs and walked towards Udyog Vihar and Sirhaul toll plaza.The disruption affected everyone – from those travelling to attend INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Delhi’ rally at Ramlila Maidan to others headed for work, hotels or home. Buses carrying rally supporters, some displaying posters of Rahul Gandhi , were also stuck in the queue.The scale of the congestion raised questions about how the checks would work on a weekday.If the enforcement drive caused such disruption on a Sunday, when regular office traffic was relatively light, Monday’s rush could put even greater pressure on the border.Thousands of commuters use this route to enter Delhi every day. Even a brief halt at the checking points can cause queues to build up over a long stretch.Police had deployed a large force near Sirhaul, including several ACPs, traffic inspectors and crime branch teams. Multiple barricades were put up on the Gurgaon side to regulate vehicles entering Delhi. Personnel stopped motorists to check registration papers, emission standards and other documents.But commuters complained that the process was holding up even vehicles that did not fall under the restricted categories. The checks led to heated exchanges between motorists and police. Sukhbir Tanwar, Congress spokesperson in Haryana, who was stranded with supporters, was seen arguing with senior officers. He alleged that the barricades were preventing people from reaching the rally.“As Rahul Gandhi is leading the protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, cops have deliberately put up barricades and are not allowing us to proceed. We have been stranded for over two hours. They are trying to kill democracy,” Tanwar told TOI.He said the buses and vehicles carrying rally participants were BS-VI compliant and that organisers had taken care to ensure they met the prescribed emission standards. “People have come from different states to join this fight for democracy. But they have been tactfully stopped,” he alleged.The delay was no less frustrating for commuters with no connection to the rally.Ramnath Kumar Yadav, a Bhondsi resident heading to Radisson Hotel, said he was stuck for nearly an hour after crossing the Udyog Vihar underpass. His destination was only a few metres away, but a queue of buses ahead of his car left him unable to move.“My vehicle has been stuck at one spot for over 40 minutes. I needed to take a left turn towards Radisson Hotel, which is barely a few metres away, but I cannot get through. Several buses are ahead of me and there is no one to help. I don’t even know why traffic has come to a halt. This is sheer harassment,” he said.Namita, a Delhi resident who had travelled to Gurgaon for official work, said she had not expected the return journey to be so difficult. “I came here for work and had no idea that getting home would turn into such a trauma. Political rallies should be organised without putting ordinary people through this. Traffic cops should have cleared the congestion quickly, but commuters are stuck in this monster jam for no fault of theirs,” she added.An earthmover stationed near the toll plaza further ate into the available road space. Its operator told TOI that work was underway to install CCTV cameras at the plaza and had been continuing for the past few days.The checking drive was part of preparations for Delhi’s new restrictions, which came into force on Nov 1 to curb air pollution. Vehicles registered outside Delhi and below BS-VI emission standards are barred from entering the capital, subject to specified exemptions. Police teams were deployed at five major entry points — Aya Nagar, Gwal Pahari, Sirhaul toll, Bajghera and Kapashera — to check compliance.Satyapal Yadav, ACP (highways) in Gurgaon, said the drive began on Sunday to familiarise motorists with the restrictions and ensure compliance. “People were informed well in advance about Delhi’s restrictions to control air pollution. Since it was a Sunday, we began the campaign today to send a clear message that violations would not be tolerated. People should have cooperated. The checks were aimed only at ensuring effective implementation of the ban in Delhi,” he added.
Article Summary: The jam was most severe on the carriageway leading to the capital, while traffic in the opposite direction flowed relatively smoothly. Buses packed with passengers were caught in the gridlock. The disruption affected everyone – from those travelling to attend INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Delhi’ rally at Ramlila Maidan.

Article Title: Bengaluru 5-star hotel tragedy: CCTV footage suggests electrical fault near pool entrance
Article Text:
The two others injured were American tourist Mathew Desantis, 41, and hotel employee Rahul Tiwari, 28.

TOI

Hotel staff get summons

T





BENGALURU: CCTV footage examined by Halasuru police investigating the deaths of two foreign nationals at Conrad Hotel’s swimming pool suggests that the suspected electrical fault may have originated near the entrance railings and steps, where LED lights are installed.The footage offers a sequence of events leading up to the Oct 30 incident, in which German national Alexander Maximilian Theiss, 57, a Lufthansa crew member, and Slovak national Juraj Horvat, 45, a project manager with IBM, died of electrocution. Police suspect that power from the lighting system or its wiring may have leaked into the pool.had reported Sunday under the headline, “Bigger tragedy averted? Current confined to 5m radius, probe finds.”A senior officer said he inspected the spot and examined the CCTV footage, which shows Theiss jumping into the pool from the opposite side and swimming towards the entrance. After covering about half the distance, he stopped briefly and then continued swimming. Horvat, meanwhile, collapsed in the water shortly after entering the pool, between 5.10pm and 5.15pm.The two others injured were American tourist Mathew Desantis, 41, and hotel employee Rahul Tiwari, 28.According to the officer, Desantis, who was already in the pool, felt an electric current while swimming but managed to get out and alert the hotel staff.Tiwari, who rushed to rescue the two men, also suffered an electric shock and is undergoing treatment. Desantis has since been discharged.Electrical inspectors, Bescom officials and police visited the pool Saturday and collected evidence. “We are waiting for reports from experts, file a final report before the court and take action against the hotel management,” the officer said.Police have begun compiling a list of hotel employees who were on duty on Oct 30. They have collected details of staff responsible for electrical maintenance, pool operations and other related work, and issued summons to some of them.“Based on the CCTV footage, there is no foul play in the deaths of the two men,” the officer said.he body of Theiss was handed over to the German consulate general after the post-mortem Sunday. Consulate officials, representatives of the airline and others were present during the procedure.Horvat’s wife, Silvia Hotuatova, who had filed a complaint in the case, returned to Slovakia Saturday night. She had stayed at the hotel after returning from the hospital and asked officials to send her husband’s body after completing the required formalities.“We are in contact with the Slovakian consulate. The post-mortem will be conducted after they give their consent, and the body will be handed over thereafter,” the officer said.
Article Summary: CCTV footage offers a sequence of events leading up to the Oct 30 incident. Police suspect that power from the lighting system or its wiring may have leaked into the pool. Theiss, 57, a Lufthansa crew member, and Horvat, 45, died of electrocution.

Article Title: Manipur ethnic conflict: Bodies of 2 missing Kuki-Zo youths found in gunny bags in Kangpokpi
Article Text:
Security forces recovered the bodies of two Kuki-Zo youths in Kangpokpi district





GUWAHATI: Security forces recovered the bodies of two Kuki-Zo youths, who went missing from Taphou Kuki village in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district on Oct 28, during a joint search operation on Sunday morning.The deceased were identified as Tinginlun Chongloi (21) and Paoginlal Hangshing (20). Their bodies were reportedly found stuffed in gunny bags in a banana plantation in Kangpokpi district.The recovery followed an extensive joint search operation by Manipur Police, CoBRA, CRPF, Assam Rifles and Rapid Action Force along SP Road, a hilly stretch east of NH-2 connecting Senapati and Kangpokpi districts.In a statement, Manipur Police said legal formalities were underway and search and combing operations would continue to identify and apprehend those responsible.Several civil society organisations in Kangpokpi have refused to claim the bodies until those responsible for the alleged abduction and killings are arrested.The killings triggered protests at the Kangpokpi district headquarters, where demonstrators alleged that the youths had been abducted and killed by ‘ Naga militants ’. Security personnel used batons and tear gas to disperse protesters gathered outside the superintendent of police’s office.Several demonstrators were reportedly injured.The Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) extended its ongoing total shutdown, which was called in protest against the alleged abduction of the two Kuki-Zo youths, in Kangpokpi by another 24 hours. The shutdown was scheduled to end at 5 pm on Sunday.The tribal body also demanded the immediate removal of deputy chief minister Losii Dikho, who belongs to the Naga community, alleging that he had failed to ensure the safe release of the youths and protect lives in the affected areas.In its list of demands, CoTU sought the extension of Kangpokpi police jurisdiction to Taphou Kuki village to strengthen security and law enforcement. It also demanded that the case be handed over to the National Investigation Agency for an independent probe and that all those involved in the alleged abduction and killings be arrested and prosecuted.The incident comes amid continuing ethnic tensions in Manipur. Five Kuki-Zo people have been killed in two separate incidents since Saturday. Three Kuki-Zo people were killed in a gunfight with Naga armed groups in Noney district on Saturday morning, hours before Meitei and Naga protesters brought Imphal to a standstill during a rally against what they described as the ‘Centre’s proxy war using Kuki SoO groups’.Deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the killings. “I am deeply saddened and shocked by the news of the brutal killings of Paoginlal Hangshing and Tinginlun Chongloi this morning, following their abduction on Oct 28. What began with hopes for their safe return has ended in a tragedy,” he said.“This heinous crime must be thoroughly investigated, and those responsible must be brought to justice without delay. The families deserve swift justice. As I had appealed earlier, I once again call upon everyone not to allow this tragedy to lead to further violence,” Kipgen added.
Article Summary: The deceased were identified as Tinginlun Chongloi (21) and Paoginlal Hangshing (20) Their bodies were reportedly found stuffed in gunny bags in a banana plantation. The killings triggered protests at the Kangpokpi district headquarters. Protesters alleged that the youths had been abducted and killed by ‘ Naga militants ’
