HYDERABAD: Women recruited from seven states for alleged commercial egg donation were being matched with prospective recipients based on specific requirements such as caste, religion, complexion, height, education and geographical background, said Malkajgiri police officials who busted a fertility racket in the city on Saturday.The accused allegedly operated a network of agents across the country who exchanged information about prospective donors through WhatsApp groups and other communication channels. Whenever couples seeking egg donors approached them with specific requirements, the agents circulated the details within their network to identify suitable women."The accused exploit women who are in need of money. They have WhatsApp groups and other means for exchanging information with a network of people across India. Whenever they receive enquiries from people looking for egg donors, the requirements are shared with illegal agents in the network,'' Begumpet inspector P Saidulu told TOI.Investigators said the prime accused, Amit Sharma, and his associates recruited women from seven different states: West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha. The accused allegedly operated under the cover of running women's hostels.Police suspect that the accommodation facilities were, in reality, being used to house prospective egg donors before they were taken to IVF centres for procedures. .Investigators said the demands of prospective recipients determined the compensation offered to donors. While some women were allegedly promised Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000, certain donors were offered as much as ₹50,000, depending on the requirements of the couples seeking eggs."The couples seeking donors specify their preferences, including complexion, caste, height and other characteristics. Based on our interactions with the accused and rescued women, complexion and regional background appear to be among the more common requirements. The agents circulate these demands within their network to identify women who match the criteria. The more specific the requirements, the higher the amount charged," an investigating officer said.Police said referrals from previous donors were a key source of recruitment. The investigation has also turned towards the role of IVF centres allegedly linked to the network. Malkajgiri DCP Ch Sridhar said police had sought clarification from health officials on the responsibility of IVF centres in verifying the identity and credentials of egg donors.
Article Summary: Malkajgiri police recently uncovered a fertility racket involving women from seven states, including West Bengal and Odisha. The accused allegedly operated a network of agents across the country who exchanged information about prospective donors through WhatsApp groups. Police suspect that the accommodation facilities were, in reality, being used to house prospective egg donors.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu plans ‘weekly ethnic wear day’ for govt employees
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu's government intends to establish a weekly ethnic wear day for all government employees

A Rajmohan





CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu govt is planning to introduce a weekly ethnic wear day for govt employees across the state.Making the announcement at Tamil Nadu Day celebrations in Chennai on Sunday, Tamil development ministersaid the move would support weavers while promoting traditional attire. Rajmohan, however, has not specified when the initiative would be introduced.“I told the chief minister that it looked like a festival on the day he wore a silk dhoti and shirt. So I suggested why not ask govt officers and staff also to wear dhoti and shirt every week for a day. The CM asked whether I had consulted with officers. When I told him they had asked me to discuss with him, CM gave the go-ahead,” Rajmohan said.The dress code would apply to his cabinet colleagues as well, Rajmohan said at the event where ministers N Anand and Aadhav Arjuna were present. Rajmohan also announced plans to set up a Tamil Sangam at the Secretariat to promote Tamil art and literature. “We will set up a Tamil Sangam and bring all other aangams under its fold. The CM will head the sangam,” he said. Efforts would also be made to organise a World Tamil Conference soon, he added.Speaking at the event, Aadhav Arjuna said Tamil Nadu should have a separate state flag, which the CM could hoist on important occasions.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi extended greetings on Tamil Nadu Day.Modi posted on X, “The hardworking and enterprising people of Tamil Nadu have made outstanding contributions to India’s progress. Tamil culture has enriched our nation’s civilisational journey in innumerable ways.” Rahul Gandhi greeted people in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and other states formed through linguistic reorganisation.Vijay said the sacrifices of those who fought to protect Tamil and unite Tamil-speaking regions would remain a guiding light for the people.DMK, however, accused TVK govt of distorting history by observing Nov 1 as Tamil Nadu Day instead of July 18.While Nov 1 marks the formation of Tamil Nadu during the linguistic reorganisation of states in 1956, July 18 marks the date in 1967 when the state was officially renamed Tamil Nadu. “Nov 1 should be celebrated not as Tamil Nadu Day but as Martyrs’ Day, in memory of those who fought to unite Tamil-speaking regions. It was on July 18 that Tamil Nadu acquired its distinct political identity,” DMK said in a statement.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu govt plans to introduce a weekly ethnic wear day for govt employees across the state. Tamil development ministersaid the move would support weavers while promoting traditional attire. Rajmohan, however, has not specified when the initiative would be introduced.

Article Title: Checked in with ‘husband’, woman found dead hours later in Faridabad hotel room
Article Text:
(AI-IMAGE) 35-year-old woman from Kharagpur, was tragically discovered dead in a hotel room in Ballabhgarh





GURGAON: A 35-year-old woman was found dead inside a hotel room in Ballabhgarh late on Saturday, with police suspecting she was strangled using a dupatta. The woman had checked into the hotel with a man who identified himself as her husband, but he was missing when hotel staff discovered her body. Police have registered a murder case and launched a search for the suspect.The deceased was identified as Chandni, who was from Kharagpur in Bihar. The man, who registered himself as Shekhar, was around 40 years old and worked as a daily wager, police said.The two checked into the hotel on Mathura Road around 10 am. They remained in the room through the day, ordering food from outside for lunch.Late at night, a hotel employee went to the room and found its door open. On entering, he saw Chandni lying motionless on the bed. She did not respond when he called out to her or tried to wake her. He alerted the hotel manager and other staff members, who informed the police.Police took the woman to a hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Her body was subsequently sent to BK Hospital for a postmortem examination. A forensic team also inspected the room and collected evidence.Ballabhgarh city police station SHO Umesh Kumar said the initial examination revealed marks on the woman’s neck, suggesting strangulation. “The cause of death would be established after the postmortem report. We have registered a murder case,” Kumar told TOI.Police said food items were found inside the room. Chandni’s family has been informed about the incident.
Article Summary: 35-year-old woman was found dead inside a hotel room in Ballabhgarh. Police suspect she was strangled using a dupatta. The woman had checked into the hotel with a man who identified himself as her husband. Police have registered a murder case and launched a search for the suspect.

Article Title: Andhra Pradesh chainsaw-wielding ‘stalker’ shot at by cops near Atmakur forest
Article Text:
Chainsaw attacker Hemanth was rushed to the Anantapur govt general hospital around 8.30pm on Sunday and was shifted to the emergency operation theatre for treatment





TIRUPATI: The 21-year-old chainsaw attacker, Hemanth , who stormed a Zilla Parishad school in Raptadu of Anantapur district and brutally attacked a Class X girl and her classmate on Saturday, was critically wounded in a police encounter near the Atmakur forest area on Sunday evening.He was rushed to the Anantapur govt general hospital around 8.30pm and was shifted to the emergency operation theatre for treatment.After the Raptadu classroom horror sent shockwaves across the country and pressure mounted on the AP govt and police for swift action, nearly 25 special police teams were formed to trace Hemanth, who fled after committing the crime. Although sources on Saturday said the accused was nabbed in Dharmavaram, police later clarified that the manhunt was still underway.Speaking to reporters at the hospital, Anantapur SP P Jagadeesh said: "Acting on credible information, when two special police teams zeroed in on Hemanth near the Atmakur forest area on Sunday evening, the accused allegedly resisted arrest, pelted stones at police personnel and tried to escape."When police fired two warning shots in the air and asked him to surrender, Hemanth tried to attack the team with a knife, injuring circle inspector Venkateswarulu, Jagadeesh added.Left with no other option, police acted in self-defence and fired six rounds at Hemanth, immobilising him, he said.Following the firing, police personnel secured Hemanth and shifted him under heavy security to the GGH for urgent medical treatment. The SP said Hemanth’s condition was critical as he sustained multiple bullet wounds below his waist. Some part of his face was also disfigured as he reportedly got injured in the forest before his encounter with police, the SP added.Around 10am on Saturday, Hemanth, armed with a chainsaw, stormed the Zilla Parishad govt school at Raptadu and attacked a 15-year-old girl in her classroom. He also attacked another classmate, who tried to save the victim from his onslaught. After both girls collapsed into a pool of blood, Hemanth abandoned the chainsaw and fled the spot.
Article Summary: Chainsaw attacker Hemanth, 21, was critically wounded in a police encounter near the Atmakur forest area on Sunday evening. He was rushed to the Anantapur govt general hospital around 8.30pm and was shifted to the emergency operation theatre for treatment. He allegedly resisted arrest, pelted stones at police personnel and tried to escape.

Article Title: Mumbai police impound BMW, seek digital media COO’s licence cancellation for ‘bid to run over’ traffic cop
Article Text:
Juhu's Juhi Mehta found herself in hot water after a parking mishap led to a collision with traffic constable





MUMBAI: Juhu police have impounded the high-end car and asked the regional transport office to cancel the driving licence of Juhu resident Juhi Mehta, who had allegedly hit vehicles and threatened a traffic constable in Vile Parle (West) last week.Mehta, chief operating officer of an online media company, was booked for threatening and obstructing traffic constable Prashant Hake (36) and driving towards him after an accident at Sangeet Mahabharati Junction on Oct 30. She was arrested the next day and later granted bail.Police said fault in the accident remained unclear. Mehta claimed she was trying to park the car to the side to prevent congestion and was uncomfortable stepping out because several people were recording the incident.Hake, attached to Santacruz Traffic Division, said he was regulating traffic near Pratiksha Bungalow in Vile Parle West on Oct 30. Between 8.15pm and 8.30pm, he noticed a crowd gathering at Sangeet Mahabharati Junction. He went to the location and found that a high-end car (driven by Mehta) and a hatchback had had a collision and were blocking traffic.He directed both drivers to move their vehicles aside to clear the obstruction.Hake alleged that Mehta argued with him, verbally abused and threatened him, and tried to leave. When he stood in front of her high-end car and repeatedly asked her to stop, she allegedly accelerated towards him. Hake moved aside and escaped without injury.Mehta allegedly drove away at high speed towards JVPD Junction. A person at the scene recorded the incident, according to the complaint. The hatchback driver, Navinkumar Udaychand Jha (42), told Hake that the high-end car had hit his vehicle from behind. Hake observed damage to its boot, bumper, right taillight, sensor lock and paintwork.Joint commissioner of police, traffic division, Satyanarayan Chaudhary said necessary action was being taken under standard operating procedures.Deputy commissioner of police (Zone West-2) Mohit Garg said further procedures were under way.
Article Summary: Juhi Mehta, chief operating officer of an online media company, was booked for threatening and obstructing traffic constable Prashant Hake. She was arrested the next day and later granted bail. Police impounded her high-end car and asked the regional transport office to cancel her licence.

Article Title: 7,000 offences in eight months: Pune records sharpest jump in drunk driving cases, police promise more patrols
Article Text:
The increase is even more alarming if one were to compare the data with 2023 figures, when only 562 cases were registered

Pune:

TOI

TOI





A policewoman suspended earlier this week for allegedly driving under the influence. A viral video that shows a drunk motorist ramming into multiple two-wheelers. Pune’s problem of drunk driving is once again back in focus, with data now showing that as many as 7,379 offences were registered within just the first eight months of this year, 12% more than last year’s entire total (6,602 cases).The increase is even more alarming if one were to compare the data with 2023 figures, when only 562 cases were registered.Police officialsspoke to said the Jan-Aug numbers are indeed worrisome. “This year’s figures exceed those of all previous years,” said additional commissioner of police, Manoj Patil. “We have been working to control drunk driving, but our efforts have to be intensified, with greater emphasis on night patrols and random checks. This is a serious offence. Lives are at risk,” he said.Residents said drunk motorists were now a common sight in the city. “Almost every evening, we see obvious signs of a vehicle being driven by someone under the influence,” said Vishal Khatir, a working professional who lives in VimannagarHe said that last month he was almost assaulted by a group travelling in a car after he confronted them. “Bystanders came to my rescue.This group stopped the car, surrounded me and threatened to beat me up. Even their speech was slurring. And I have hardly ever seen police patrols in the area,” he said.Animesh Sherkha, a Koregaon Park resident, said drunk driving was commonplace in the area, despite police presence. “It’s indeed a problem, given the number of bars and restaurants here. It’s unfortunate that even after the Porsche incident (in 2024), city police have been unable to clamp down.”A retired RTO officialspoke to said a critical countermeasure could be cancellation of driving licences. “Just last month, the police actually recommended suspension or cancellation of around 1,700 driving licences for serious traffic violations, including drunk driving. In my view, the state government should consider allowing authorities to permanently cancel the licences of anyone caught driving under the influence, without the possibility of reissuance,” the retired official said, adding that such measures could be backed by tougher penalties, including vehicle confiscation, higher fines and imprisonment.Harshad Abhyankar, a member of the Save Pune Traffic Movement said it was time enforcement moved beyond routine checks and fines. “Drink driving is often treated as an issue of indiscipline, prompting the usual suggestions of increased surveillance and higher fines. A dedicated campaign over several months can help curb the problem, but authorities also need to think differently and explore innovative measures,” he said.Salunke Vihar Road resident Atul Pirodkar highlighted another concern: open drinking near liquor shops. “A good example is the shop near my house. I see people drinking in the open every day. Surely, the police are aware of the problem. Residents of NIBM Road Annexe, barely 3 km away, have also been complaining about late-evening disturbances caused by people under the influence of alcohol,” he said.
Article Summary: As many as 7,379 offences were registered within just the first eight months of this year. This is 12% more than last year’s entire total (6,602 cases) The increase is even more alarming if one were to compare the data with 2023 figures, when only 562 cases were registered.

Article Title: Ludhiana man stabs wife to death days after returning from Australia, son sent out to buy milk
Article Text:
Victims Kamal; Son Gagandeep at murder spot (R)





LUDHIANA: Two days after returning from Australia, a man allegedly stabbed his wife to death at their house in Vikas Nagar on Pakhowal Road. Police said the man suspected his wife of infidelity and stabbed her multiple times in the stomach and neck with a kitchen knife. Before committing the murder, the man sent their son to the market to get milk.The victim was identified as Kamaldeep Kaur, 49, and the accused as her husband, Ravinder Singh , 50, who works as a pick-up van driver. Dugri police have apprehended the accused.The incident occurred late Saturday when the couple was at home with their elder son, Gagandeep Singh. Their younger son lives in Australia, and the couple had gone there to meet him. While Kamaldeep had returned about four months ago, Ravinder returned to India two days ago.Gagandeep said that his parents had been behaving normally for the past two days and had not fought. Late Saturday, his father asked him to get milk from the market. He left the house and, on returning, saw his father running out of the house. When he asked what had happened, his father told him to go inside and check.Gagandeep rushed inside and saw his mother lying on the bed in a pool of blood.He raised an alarm and sought help from neighbours to rush his mother to the hospital. The woman was taken to the hospital, where doctors declared her dead.Inspector Gurmukh Singh, SHO of Dugri police station, said, "The accused used a kitchen knife to stab his wife to death. He attacked her in the stomach and neck multiple times. The police suspect that the man had returned to India with a plan to kill his wife as he executed the murder two days after his return."The inspector added that a murder case had been registered against the accused, who had been taken into custody. Initial investigations suggest that suspicion of infidelity was the motive behind the murder. The accused is being interrogated.
Article Summary: Man suspected his wife of infidelity and stabbed her multiple times in the stomach and neck with a kitchen knife. Victim identified as Kamaldeep Kaur, 49, and the accused as Ravinder Singh, 50, who works as a pick-up van driver. Police suspect that the man had returned to India with a plan to kill his wife.

Article Title: Punjab ASI caught on CCTV planting drugs at Shiv Sena neta's house; suspended, SIT probe ordered
Article Text:
Police have suspended an assistant sub-inspector and initiated a special investigation team inquiry after disturbing footage emerged.





KHANNA: Police have suspended an assistant sub-inspector and ordered a special investigation team (SIT) inquiry after hidden-camera footage allegedly showed him planting drugs at the house of a local Shiv Sena functionary.The disciplinary action followed the public release of home security footage recorded at the house of Mahant Kashmir Giri. The video appears to show an officer in plainclothes hiding a package beneath a bedroom mattress shortly before a uniformed police team enters the room to "seize" the evidence.Khanna's senior superintendent of police, Darpan Ahluwalia, confirmed the officer's suspension and the formation of a formal investigation panel led by an officer of SP rank."We have taken cognisance of the packets contents and all aspects of the case are being examined." Ahluwalia said, adding that: "The drug accused was discharged and the police personnel suspended with immediate effect."Ahluwalia said: "I would also like to make it clear to the people of Khanna and Punjab that accountability of Punjab Police is of utmost importance in the ongoing Yudh Nashean Virudh (war against drugs) campaign.The law is supreme, irrespective of whether the person involved is an accused, a drug smuggler, or a police personnel."She added that Punjab Police maintains a zero-tolerance stance regarding illegal activities, corruption, and police misconduct in cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.A senior police officer confirmed that a parallel departmental inquiry is in progress with investigators attempting to establish the origin of the drug allegedly placed inside the house.
Article Summary: Police have suspended an assistant sub-inspector and ordered a special investigation team (SIT) inquiry after hidden-camera footage allegedly showed him planting drugs. The disciplinary action followed the public release of home security footage recorded at the house of Mahant Kashmir Giri. The video appears to show an officer in plainclothes hiding a package beneath a bedroom mattress.

Article Title: UP man gouges out wife's eye, crushes her face with brick before hanging self over domestic row; kids return from fair to find bodies
Article Text:
In a shocking incident in Hardoi district's Pali area, Lalput Rathore allegedly killed his wife, Janki





LUCKNOW: A 52-year-old man allegedly murdered his wife by gouging out her right eye with a knife and then crushing her face and head with a brick before dying by suicide at their home in Hardoi district's Pali area late Saturday, police said.The incident came to light when the couple's children returned from a local fair and found both parents dead in separate rooms.The deceased were identified as Lalput Rathore and his wife, Janki (50). The incident took place around 11:30pm. Preliminary investigation suggests the couple had an argument linked to a long-standing domestic dispute.Police suspect Lalput, who allegedly doubted his wife's character, attacked her with a knife, inflicting fatal injuries on her abdomen. He then allegedly struck her head and face with a brick, killing her on the spot.After the attack, Lalput went to another room and hanged himself, police said.The crime came to light when the couple's eight-year-old son, Pushpendra, returned from the fair and found his mother lying in a pool of blood. Family members then searched for Lalput and found his body hanging from a noose in another room. The children's cries drew neighbours, who rushed to the house and alerted police.Police recovered a blood-stained knife and a brick, believed to have been used in the killing. Both bodies were sent for post-mortem examination.Neighbours told police that Lalput frequently quarrelled with Janki and allegedly assaulted her, particularly after consuming alcohol. A local resident also claimed that frequent visitors to the house, purportedly linked to Lalput's alleged involvement in illicit liquor sales, often fuelled his suspicions and triggered arguments.The couple had eight children, including six sons and two daughters. Three of the sons work outside the village as labourers, while the younger children lived with their parents, said circle officer Santosh Singh.
Article Summary: Lalput Rathore, 52, allegedly gouged out his wife Janki's right eye with a knife. He then allegedly crushed her head and face with a brick, killing her on the spot. The couple's children returned from a local fair and found both parents dead in separate rooms.

Article Title: AAP MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh resigns from Punjab assembly
Article Text:
Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, an Aam Aadmi Party MLA, has resigned from the Punjab Legislative Assembly.





AMRITSAR: The internal turmoil in the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) refuses to die down, after AAP MLA from Amritsar North Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh resigned from the Punjab Legislative Assembly.In the recent past, two sitting party MLAs—Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanaur—have also resigned from the party's primary membership.In a one-line resignation letter uploaded on his Facebook page, on Monday , Kunwar, a former IPS officer, wrote to the Speaker of the Punjab Vidhan Sabha: “I hereby tender my resignation of my seat in the House with effect from 1.11.2026.” The resignation had been sent through email, WhatsApp and post.In an accompanying message addressed to the public, Kunwar said he would remain indebted to the people until his last breath for the love and respect they had bestowed upon him.He claimed that he had achieved 90 per cent of the targets he had set for himself as an MLA and had provided area-wise details of the works undertaken by him. He also said he had always raised the voice of Amritsar and fearlessly taken up its issues.Kunwar further claimed that his greatest achievement had been helping end the 'mai-baap' culture in politics and working with the people as his source of inspiration.However, he gave no clear indication of his future political plans except saying only that his objective would be to work with the people in shaping the strategy ahead and ensuring clean politics and transparent, efficient governance.Notably, in June last year, the party had suspended Kunwar for five years over alleged anti-party activities. The decision was taken by the party's Political Affairs Committee.Kunwar was also not inducted into the Punjab Cabinet after the formation of the AAP government led by Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann.
Article Summary: Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, an Aam Aadmi Party MLA, has resigned from the Punjab Legislative Assembly. The resignation had been sent through email, WhatsApp and post. In June last year, the party had suspended Kunwar for five years over alleged anti-party activities.

Article Title: Months before taking control of hundreds of fridges at French supermarkets, did hackers break into the US army freezers; Pentagon classifies it as ...
Article Text:
What happened in France

Food and Agriculture Information Sharing and Analysis Center's warning

The Pentagon is investigating whether a cyberattack triggered a series of commercial freezer failures that spoiled food across multiple US military bases in August, according to a US official familiar with the matter. The disruptions hit approximately six commissaries -- the on-base grocery stores serving service members and their families -- the official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss an ongoing probe. At Fort Huachuca in Arizona, base officials discovered that a walk-in freezer had unexpectedly shifted into defrost mode, heating its inventory and ruining the stored provisions.The US Cyber Command and Defense Department law enforcement agencies are leading the inquiry. Investigators have not publicly identified any suspects or formally confirmed the technical root cause behind the equipment failures. Reuters first reported Thursday that investigators were treating the incidents as a possible hack. It’s unclear who might be responsible or whether investigators have conclusively determined what caused the failures.The US investigators are also coordinating with French authorities.Earlier this month, hackers manipulated temperature controls on commercial cooling systems across more than 350 locations in France, forcing widespread inventory disposal at local supermarkets.In early October, hackers targeted hundreds of French supermarkets in a cyberattack that reportedly caused refrigerators and freezers to overheat, spoiling food and sparking fires.Fridges at French supermarket chains Carrefour, Monoprix, the Les Mousquetaires-owned Intermarche, and Cooperative U, among others, all saw fridges heat up to as much as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight. The incident highlights growing vulnerabilities in operational technology—the internet-connected industrial control systems that regulate everyday supply chain infrastructure. While critical infrastructure discussions often center on power grids and water treatment facilities, cybersecurity analysts warn that food storage systems frequently rely on remote-access controls protected by weak defenses.The Food and Agriculture Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC), an industry threat-intelligence group, has repeatedly warned that internet-accessible industrial controls present an easy target for malicious actors. Because the food sector cannot tolerate extended downtime without severe financial and logistical losses, facilities remain prime targets for extortion and ransomware campaigns. A 2021 Department of Homeland Security assessment similarly warned that cyber-induced refrigeration failures posed direct risks to national food distribution networks.The August commissary failures were first noted publicly by the Signal and Silence blog, followed by reporting from Stars and Stripes on the military's involvement and The Telegraph on international coordination with France.In Congress, the incidents have renewed momentum around supply chain security. Lawmakers reintroduced the bipartisan Farm and Food Cybersecurity Act in 2025, aiming to bolster crisis response protocols and federal threat-sharing mechanisms across the nation’s agricultural and distribution pipelines.
Article Summary: The Pentagon is investigating whether a cyberattack triggered a series of commercial freezer failures that spoiled food across multiple US military bases in August. The disruptions hit approximately six commissaries -- the on-base grocery stores serving service members and their families. The US Cyber Command and Defense Department law enforcement agencies are leading the inquiry.

Article Title: 5 from Bengal, 2 from UP among 8 still missing in Uttarakhand's Kedartal after avalanche; 2 Helicopter searches fail to trace group due to heavy snowfall
Article Text:
The group had left Gangotri for Kedartal on Oct 27 but became stranded following an avalanche.





UTTARKASHI: Eight people, including seven trekkers and a guide, remained missing in the Kedartal region of Uttarkashi on Sunday, three days after an avalanche blocked their return route.Two helicopter sorties failed to locate the group or their tents, while heavy snowfall and the threat of further avalanches hampered rescue operations.Authorities deployed another State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) mountaineering team with specialised equipment to intensify the search, officials said.The missing trekkers were identified as Tapas Bauri, Ratan Ghosh, Manoj Khovas, Rintu Mandal and Uday Ghosh, all from West Bengal, and Deepika Verma and Vartika Verma from Uttar Pradesh. Their guide, Siddharth Rana, a resident of Uttarkashi, was also missing.Gangotri National Park deputy director Mayank Garg told TOI that rescue teams had found no trace of the eight despite continuing search efforts.The group had left Gangotri for Kedartal on Oct 27 but became stranded after an avalanche struck the trekking route on Oct 29.Four porters who had moved ahead of the trekkers managed to return safely to Gangotri, while the remaining eight could not make their way back.Saurav Panwar of trekking agency Soul Seekers said heavy snowfall on Oct 29 had prevented the group from returning.The agency alerted the administration on the morning of Oct 30, but helicopter rescue operations began only late on Oct 31, he claimed.Panwar said an earlier rescue attempt might have improved the chances of bringing the group back safely.Meanwhile, the agency sent its own rescue team towards Kedartal.The rescuers managed to spot the stranded group’s tent but had to turn back about a kilometre short of the location because of deep snow and the risk of another avalanche.With the ground route inaccessible, the agency sought a helicopter evacuation.However, two aerial reconnaissance sorties conducted on Sunday failed to locate either the tent or any of the missing people. The eight remained unaccounted for as rescue teams prepared to continue the search amid difficult weather and terrain conditions.
Article Summary: The group had left Gangotri for Kedartal on Oct 27 but became stranded after an avalanche struck the trekking route on Oct 29. Two helicopter sorties failed to locate the group or their tents, while heavy snowfall and the threat of further avalanches hampered rescue operations.

Article Title: Dia Mirza row divides Mumbai civic leadership: Mayor seeks say in BMC campaigns, deputy mayor backs actor
Article Text:
Mayor, deputy mayor differ over Dia Mirza's Diwali appeal

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the BMC's pollution-free Diwali campaign featuring Dia Mirza? Yes, it's a great initiative. No, I disagree with it. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MUMBAI: A row over the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation ’s (BMC) pollution-free Diwali campaign featuring actor Dia Mirza has exposed a difference of opinion within Mumbai’s civic leadership, with Mayor Ritu Tawde seeking approval over future celebrity campaigns while Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi backing the actor’s appeal against bursting firecrackers.Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde has said the names of celebrities roped in for civic campaigns must be brought to her notice and cleared by her in future.Addressing the media on Monday, Tawde said she was unaware that actor Dia Mirza had been roped in for the campaign. She said she would raise the issue with the civic administration and insist that the names of celebrities associated with BMC campaigns be communicated to her in advance.Tawde also criticised Mirza, describing her as anti-Hindu, and said she opposed those who had spoken against Prime Minister Narendra Modi or any of his campaigns in the past.“Those who oppose Hindutva, we will oppose them. Henceforth, the BMC should not make any public statement without my approval,” she said.Referring to Mumbai BJP president Ameet Satam’s social media post opposing the campaign, Tawde said it reflected the position of all BJP corporators.She added that while Mirza was free to post on her personal social media handles, content published through the BMC’s official handles should not go out without the ruling party’s approval.The controversy erupted after the civic body’s anti-firecracker appeal featuring Mirza came under criticism from the BJP leadership, leading to questions over the removal of the actor’s message from the BMC’s social media handles.However, Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi disagreed with the objections raised against the actor’s appeal. Ghadi said he did not believe Mirza had said anything wrong in urging citizens to avoid firecrackers and questioned the need to remove her message.He also said there was no reason for Satam or Tawde to oppose the appeal.
Article Summary: Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde has said the names of celebrities roped in for civic campaigns must be brought to her notice and cleared by her in future. Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi disagreed with the objections raised against the actor’s appeal.

Article Title: Delhi Police personnel stage protest at PHQ over transfer of ACP, SHO
Article Text:
In view of the growing tension, security arrangements around the headquarters were subsequently strengthened





NEW DELHI: Several Delhi Police personnel staged a protest at the Delhi Police Headquarters (PHQ) against the transfer of the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) and the Station House Officer (SHO) of Shahdara district.The transfers followed protests by lawyers, who accused the two officers of misbehaviour and alleged that the ACP had brandished his pistol during an altercation. In a striking turn of events, the ACP whose transfer had sparked the demonstration was himself leading the protest, adding an unusual dimension to the incident.The demonstration unfolded in two phases, with the first gathering taking place outside the Delhi Police Headquarters, followed by a second protest within the premises.Several police personnel assembled to express their opposition to the transfer orders, signalling their dissatisfaction with the departmental action taken against the two officers following the allegations levelled by lawyers.During the demonstration, a Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) approached the protesting personnel and attempted to pacify them. He urged them not to stage a protest or behave like demonstrators, reminding them that they were members of the police force.However, his intervention failed to persuade the personnel, who continued their protest.In view of the growing tension, security arrangements around the headquarters were subsequently strengthened. Additional police personnel were deployed, particularly at Gate No. 1, to maintain law and order and prevent any untoward incident. Paramilitary personnel were also stationed in the area as a precautionary measure.One of the last major instances of such a demonstration was witnessed in November 2019, when police personnel took to the streets following clashes between policemen and lawyers at Tis Hazari Court.
Article Summary: Several Delhi Police personnel staged a protest against the transfer of the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) and the Station House Officer (SHO) of Shahdara district. The transfers followed protests by lawyers, who accused the two officers of misbehaviour. Article Title: 'Always been anti-Hindu': Mumbai mayor's jibe at Dia Mirza after BMC removes Diwali campaign video; actor responds
Article Text:
BMC decided to pull Dia Mirza's video from its pollution-free Diwali campaign

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with the BMC's decision to remove Dia Mirza's video from the pollution-free Diwali campaign? Yes, it was justified. No, it was unfair. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Dia Mirza reacts after BMC removes Diwali campaign video

Opposition questions BMC's decision

Nitesh Rane questions Dia Mirza's stand on other religious festivals





MUMBAI: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has removed actor Dia Mirza’s video from its pollution-free Diwali campaign after Mumbai BJP chief Ameet Satam objected to her inclusion, triggering a political row, with Mayor Ritu Tawde calling the actor “anti-Hindu” and saying she had been blacklisted.Mirza, who had appealed to citizens to avoid bursting firecrackers and celebrate an environment-friendly Diwali, questioned the criticism of a campaign based on public interest and the Bombay High Court’s directives.Speaking to ANI, she said, “Why should anyone be critical of a video that the Honourable Bombay High Court and BMC have made me record in public interest? Air Pollution is an area of concern and all efforts to reduce pollution should be welcomed because its a matter of public health.”The BMC had launched the campaign amid rising air pollution in Mumbai, urging citizens to celebrate Diwali in an environment-friendly manner in line with a Bombay High Court directive.Several celebrities were roped in to spread the message, including Mirza, actors Madhuri Dixit and Nishigandha Wad, and cricketer Ajinkya Rahane.However, Mirza’s clip was removed from the civic body’s social media pages on Sunday after Satam objected to her inclusion in a post on X, tagging the BMC’s official account.“We don't need lessons on how to celebrate #Diwali from @deespeak. Our traditions are deeply rooted in our culture,” Satam wrote.Within hours of his post, the BMC, led by Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide, removed Mirza’s video.Campaign videos featuring Madhuri Dixit, Nishigandha Wad and Ajinkya Rahane continued to remain on the civic body’s X and Instagram pages.Reacting to the controversy, Mirza said in a social media post, “Koi paise nahi liye hain. Bhalai ka zamana hee nahi raha (I did not charge (BMC) any fee (for the Diwali campaign). There is no goodness left in this era).”The BMC’s post accompanying her video had stated that, in accordance with the High Court’s directives, bursting firecrackers on public roads, lanes and footpaths was strictly prohibited.Mayor Ritu Tawde defended the removal of the video and made remarks against the actor on Monday. “Dia Mirza has always sided with divisive forces. She had trolled PM Modi on the NEET exam issue,” Tawde told reporters.“She has always been anti-Hindu. We have blacklisted her,” the mayor added.Opposition leaders criticised the civic body for taking down Mirza’s clip, questioning whether the administration had acted under political pressure.Shiv Sena (UBT) spokesperson and former Mumbai mayor Kishori Pednekar asked whether the civic administration had “become a slave of the BJP or its Mumbai president”.Alleging that Satam’s interference in the civic body’s day-to-day functioning was increasing, Pednekar said the administration should not have succumbed to what she termed the BJP leader’s “communal agenda”.MNS corporator Yashwant Killedar also criticised Satam, saying that if the BJP Mumbai president was so fond of firecrackers, party office-bearers should burst as many crackers as they wished outside his residence.“Our Diwali can be celebrated even by lighting a single lamp and a lantern. Does the BJP approve of Satam's brand of 'hypocritical Hindutva' that supports bursting firecrackers in the name of religion?” he asked.BJP minister Nitesh Rane also criticised Mirza, questioning why she had spoken about pollution during Diwali but had not offered similar advice during other religious festivals.“Dia Mirza tweeted about Diwali, but she never tweets or offers such advice during Eid, Muharram or Bakri Eid,” he said.“People like her are against the Sanatan Hindu religion. I will discuss this issue with CM Fadnavis and focus on preventing such matters in the future,” Rane added.Shiv Sena spokesperson Shaina NC, meanwhile, said Mirza should know the significance of Diwali and the need to be mindful of pollution.“Dia Mirza, whose name itself means light, should know that the Festival of Lights refers to Diwali. Everyone knows the need to be mindful of pollution and avoid bursting firecrackers,” she said.Union minister Ramdas Athawale said the issue should not be linked to any particular community, while underlining the right of every religion to celebrate its festivals.“Dia Mirza belongs to the Muslim community, but this is not a matter of any particular community. In India, the Constitution given by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar grants every religion the right to celebrate its festivals,” he said.“Just as Muslims celebrate Eid and observe Ramadan, members of the Hindu community also participate in these celebrations. If firecrackers are not burst, Diwali may lose some of its significance. However, we must also be concerned about excessive pollution,” Athawale added.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: BMC has removed actor Dia Mirza’s video from its pollution-free Diwali campaign. Mumbai BJP chief Ameet Satam objected to her inclusion, triggering a political row. Mayor Ritu Tawde called the actor “anti-Hindu’ and said she had been blacklisted. Mirza, who had appealed to citizens to avoid bursting firecrackers, questioned the criticism of the campaign.

Article Title: ​​Ban on drones, paragliders & hot air balloons in Sambhajinagar for 60 days
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar police commissionerate has imposed a 60-day ban on the flying of drones and other aerial devices across its jurisdiction, citing security threats to VVIPs and public safety concerns arising from possible misuse by anti-national elements.As per the prohibitory order issued under section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, the flying of drones, remote-controlled microlight aircraft, paragliders, paramotors, hand gliders and hot air balloons will remain prohibited across the entire commissionerate area from Nov 3 to Jan 2 next year.“Such devices can be used to attack VVIPs, endanger human lives, damage public property and disturb law and order, and therefore it is necessary to initiate preventive and prohibitive measures. Only aerial surveillance by police and any drone operations undertaken with specific permission of the police commissioner will be exempted from the ban,” said the order.The commissionerate has stated that any person violating the order will be liable for punishment under section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar police commissionerate said: “As it is not possible to serve notice individually to all persons concerned, the order has been passed ex-parte and is being publicized through the media and by displaying copies on notice boards at the offices of the police commissioner, deputy commissioners of police, assistant commissioners of police, all police stations, traffic branches, sub-divisional offices and beat outposts. ”
Article Summary: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar police commissionerate has imposed a 60-day ban on the flying of drones and other aerial devices across its jurisdiction. The commissionerate cites security threats to VVIPs and public safety concerns arising from possible misuse by anti-national elements.

Article Title: HC quashes murder case against man, says delayed witness statements recorded with 'mala fide intention'
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: The Aurangabad bench of Bombay High Court has quashed an FIR and a subsequent sessions court case against a man in a Diwali banner-dispute murder case. Between 30 and 35 people were named as accused in the FIR, which was registered at Bidkin police station in Oct 2025.The high court specifically observed that the statements of two eyewitnesses were recorded after a 30-day delay with “mala fide intention” to falsely implicate the applicant, Akash Ashok Vanjare, by assigning him a more incriminating role.Justice Sushil M. Ghodeswar allowed the criminal application filed by Vanjare and set aside the FIR registered at Bidkin, the chargesheet, and Paithan Sessions Court’s March 28, 2026, order issuing process against him. The order was originally passed on Oct 15 and modified on Oct 28 following a plea for speaking to the minutes.The FIR was registered on Oct 24, 2025, under Sections 103(1), 189(2), 190, and 191(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Sections 45 and 51 were later added in the chargesheet, and the matter is currently pending as a sessions case.According to the prosecution, a dispute over banners escalated into violence on Oct 23, 2025.Rutik Dharme had put up a Diwali greeting banner near Shivaji Maharaj statue on Oct 20. On Oct 22, Rishikesh alias Chiman Jadhav put up his birthday banner in front of it. The complainant alleged that Vanjare and another individual, Waman Sathe, had instructed Jadhav to place the banner there, a claim based on information passed to the complainant by one Kiran Gujar.The following night, a mob of 30 to 35 persons armed with iron rods, pipes, and sticks allegedly attacked the complainant’s group. Tanmay Ganesh Chormare was struck on the head with an iron rod and succumbed to his injuries on Oct 24.Vanjare’s counsel, advocate Sandeep Rajebhosale, argued that his client was neither present at the spot nor part of the assault or unlawful assembly. He further contended that merely asking for a banner to be put up could not amount to the abetment of murder.The state opposed the plea. Additional public prosecutor A. A. A. Khan cited the statements of witnesses Somnath Tupe and Amol Gade, recorded on Nov 20, 2025, which alleged that the applicant had exhorted the assailants to attack members of the Dhangar community. Advocate Rashmi Kulkarni, appearing for the complainant, also relied on these statements alongside Sections 45 and 51 of the BNS.However, the high court noted that these statements were recorded nearly a month after the incident. They were introduced only after the co-accused had been granted anticipatory bail and the applicant had moved a bail application before the sessions court. The bench observed that despite the presence of “so many eyewitnesses” at the scene, the applicant’s alleged role was not established in any earlier accounts.“The minimum role attributed to him, as stated in the FIR, is that of asking Rushikesh alias Chiman Jadhav to fix the banner,” the high court said, concluding that this act could not amount to abetment and did not attract Sections 45 and 51 of the BNS. It held that the investigating officer had recorded the two delayed statements with a mala fide intention to falsely implicate the applicant.Noting that the high court’s inherent powers under Section 482 of the CrPC are to be used sparingly but are vital to prevent the abuse of the judicial process and secure the ends of justice, Justice Ghodeswar held that neither the FIR nor the subsequent statements disclosed a cognisable offence against the applicant.
Article Summary: The Aurangabad bench of Bombay High Court has quashed an FIR and a subsequent sessions court case against a man in a Diwali banner-dispute murder case. The high court specifically observed that the statements of two eyewitnesses were recorded after a 30-day delay with “mala fide intention” to falsely implicate the applicant.

Article Title: Bangladeshi national gets 2-year jail term for illegal stay in India
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A Jalna court has sentenced a 26-year-old Bangladeshi national to two years’ simple imprisonment for illegally entering and residing in India using forged identity documents, including Aadhaar, PAN and voter ID cards.Additional sessions judge R B Parvekar of the Jalna District and Sessions Court-6 convicted Aslam Mani Kaji in a case registered by Badnapur police. Kaji pleaded guilty during the trial, following which the court convicted and sentenced him.The court awarded him two years’ simple imprisonment under sections 14 and 14A(b) of the Foreigners Act, besides shorter sentences under the Passport (Entry into India) Rules. All substantive sentences will run concurrently, making the effective prison term two years.The court also directed the prosecution to initiate Kaji’s deportation after completion of the sentence and submit a compliance report. The period spent in custody since April 7, 2025, will be set off against the sentence.According to the prosecution, Kaji and co-accused Bulbuli Mustfur Rahman allegedly entered India illegally from Bangladesh and procured forged identity documents to establish their identity.The duo initially lived in Dombivli before moving to Badnapur in Jalna district.The case surfaced on April 7, 2025, when Badnapur police responded to a Dial 112 call reporting a possible assault and threat to life at Noor Hospital. Police found a man and woman arguing at the hospital. During questioning, they initially claimed to be from Mumbai, but further inquiry revealed they were Bangladeshi nationals, leading to registration of the case.The investigation was conducted by sub-inspector A G Jaiswal of Badnapur police station, who later filed the chargesheet. The court said the trial against the second accused, Bulbuli Mustfur Rahman, will continue in accordance with law.Additional public prosecutor Adv Jayshree B Solanke (Borade) represented the prosecution.
Article Summary: Aslam Mani Kaji, 26, was convicted in a case registered by Badnapur police. Kaji pleaded guilty during the trial, following which the court convicted and sentenced him. The trial against the second accused, Bulbuli Mustfur Rahman, will continue.

Article Title: Sena (UBT) workers ‘inaugurate’ Nanded hospital a day before Eknath Shinde’s official event
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A day before deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde ’s scheduled inauguration of a newly built 100-bed govt hospital in Nanded ’s Wadi area, Shiv Sena (UBT) workers on Saturday held a symbolic inauguration of the facility, escalating the political tussle between the rival Sena factions.Partyworkers broke coconuts and showered flowers and gulal at the hospital, claiming the project was conceived, sanctioned and completed during Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) govt’s tenure and that Mahayuti was attempting to claim credit for it.“The project was sanctioned and funded by MVA govt due to the efforts of then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray . The foundation stone of the hospital was laid by Aaditya Thackeray . Now, an attempt is being made to take credit for ready-made work by holding a fresh inauguration,” said Sunil Kadam, Shiv Sena (UBT) Nanded taluka chief.Local Sena (UBT) politicians said they acted on instructions from party chief Uddhav Thackeray and inaugurated the facility before the official programme.“The facility was ready but waiting for inauguration. The delay was causing huge inconvenience to rural patients. Also, the rival camp was making a big inauguration event by spending public money. This is unacceptable during the current drought conditions.The same money can be offered to farmers now,” Kadam said.He claimed police had contacted him over the incident but said no offence had been registered against him till Saturday evening.The 100-bed hospital is scheduled to be formally inaugurated on Sunday by Shinde.Local Shiv Sena MLA Balaji Kalyankar, who was earlier associated with the Thackeray faction, could not be reached for comment.The episode is expected to further sharpen the rivalry between the two Shiv Sena factions over credit for development projects in the district.
Article Summary: Partyworkers broke coconuts and showered flowers and gulal at the hospital. They claim the project was conceived, sanctioned and completed during Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) govt’s tenure. The 100-bed hospital is scheduled to be formally inaugurated on Sunday by Shinde.

Article Title: Will topple Dharashiv ZP in six months if Sena members treated as slaves: Tanaji Sawant
Article Text:
Tanaji Sawant

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Cracks within Mahayuti have come out into the open in Dharashiv, with Shiv Sena MLA and former minister Tanaji Sawant on Friday issuing a stern warning to BJP MLA Rana Jagjitsinh Patil and Dharashiv Zilla Parishad (ZP) president Archana Patil over the functioning of the civic body. He even threatened to topple the ruling arrangement within six months if the situation continued.Sawant alleged that BJP was running the ZP in an arbitrary and dictatorial manner, warning that Shiv Sena would not tolerate its elected representatives being treated as “bonded labourers” or “slaves” and threatened to topple the ruling arrangement within six months if the situation continued.Addressing Shiv Sena ZP members, Sawant urged them to resist any attempt to sideline or dominate them. “We are not bonded labourers. This dispensation has come to power because of our support. Power does not belong to one party alone. We are equal stakeholders. If anyone tries to treat our members like slaves and dictate terms, refuse to work and register your protest. We will not tolerate arrogance of power. If our members continue to be treated this way, we will bring down govt within six months,” he said.Sawant emphasised the role of elected representatives and said ZP members, and not a handful of individuals, should drive decision-making, while the chief executive officer should play an advisory role.“The ZP members will decide how the body functions, while the CEO’s role is to guide them. Do not tolerate injustice. Focus on development work and tackling the drought situation,” he told party workers.The sharp remarks come amid growing friction between BJP and deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena in Dharashiv. Differences between the alliance partners, which had surfaced during the recent graduate constituency election-related developments, now appear to have spilled over into the administration of the zilla parishad, casting a shadow over the local power-sharing arrangement.In another warning, Sawant said Shiv Sena would respond “in its own style” if farmers from his Paranda assembly constituency were harassed by banks, financial institutions or recovery agents over loan repayments.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena MLA Tanaji Sawant issues stern warning to BJP MLA Rana Jagjitsinh Patil and Dharashiv Zilla Parishad president Archana Patil over the functioning of the civic body. He even threatened to topple the ruling arrangement within six months if the situation continued.
